translations.idiomatic: In conduct my brother served his parents filially and his elder brother obediently; he never scolded even servants—truly a gentleman who never lost composure or spoke harshly to others.

sentences.zh: 沖和淹通，內有皁白，舉動尺寸，吾每咨之。

translations.literal: Mild and harmonious, steeped and penetrating, inwardly possessing black and white; in every movement's measure I always consulted him.
translations.idiomatic: Mild and penetrating, inwardly discerning right from wrong—in every movement's measure I always consulted him.

sentences.zh: 常云：「兄文骨氣，可推英麗以自許。

translations.literal: He often said: "Elder brother's literary bone and breath can be extended to heroic beauty for self-commendation."
translations.idiomatic: He often said, "Brother, your writing has true bone and spirit—you may claim heroic beauty for yourself."

sentences.zh: 又兄為人矯介欲過，宜每中和。

translations.literal: Again elder brother as a man is upright and exacting almost to excess—you ought each time to harmonize the center.
translations.idiomatic: Again, brother, you are upright and exacting almost to excess—you ought always to seek the mean."

sentences.zh: 」道此猶在耳，萬世不復一見，奈何！

translations.literal: These words are still in the ear—ten thousand generations will not see him once again—what can be done!
translations.idiomatic: These words are still in my ears—never in ten thousand generations shall I see him again—what can be done!

sentences.zh: 唯十紙手跡，封拆儼然，至於思戀不可懷。

translations.literal: Only ten sheets of handwriting, sealed and opened still intact—as for longing and remembrance, it cannot be held in the breast.
translations.idiomatic: Only ten sheets in his hand remain, sealed and opened as if yesterday—as for longing, it cannot be borne in the heart.

sentences.zh: 及聞吾病，肝心寸絕，謂當以幅巾薄葬之事累汝，奈何反相殯送！

translations.literal: When he heard of my illness his liver and heart broke inch by inch; he said he would burden you with the matter of headcloth and simple burial—how could it be that instead you bore each other in funeral escort!
translations.idiomatic: When he heard I was ill his heart broke inch by inch; he said he would burden you with arranging a simple burial in plain cloth—how could it be that instead you bore him to the grave!

sentences.zh: 弟由來意謂：「婦人雖無子，不宜踐二庭。

translations.literal: Younger brother from of old meant: "Though a woman has no son, she ought not tread two courts."
translations.idiomatic: Brother had long held that "though a woman has no son, she ought not enter a second household."

sentences.zh: 此風若行，便可家有孝婦」。

translations.literal: If this wind is practiced, then every house can have a filial wife."
translations.idiomatic: If this custom prevailed, every house could have a filial wife."

sentences.zh: 仲長《昌言》，亦其大要。

translations.literal: Zhongchang's Open Words also states its great essentials.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongchang Tong's Open Words also states the same essentials.

sentences.zh: 劉新婦以刑傷自誓，必留供養；

translations.literal: Liu the new wife by cutting and wounding vowed herself, surely to remain for provision;
translations.idiomatic: Liu the new wife vowed by self-injury to remain and provide for the household;

sentences.zh: 殷太妃感柏舟之節，不奪其志。

translations.literal: Lady Yin the Grand Consort, moved by the integrity of Cypress Boat, did not wrest away her resolve.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Consort Yin, moved by the integrity of Cypress Boat, did not override her resolve.

sentences.zh: 僕射篤順，范夫人知禮，求得左率第五兒，廬位有主。

translations.literal: The Vice Director was sincere and obedient, Lady Fan knew ritual; they sought the fifth son of the Left Commander—the mourning hut had a master.
translations.idiomatic: The Vice Director was sincere and obedient, Lady Fan knew ritual; they sought the fifth son of the Left Commander—the mourning place had its master.

sentences.zh: 此亦何益冥然之痛，為是存者意耳。

translations.literal: This also what use for dark pain—it is only the intent of those who remain.
translations.idiomatic: This also does nothing for pain in the darkness—it is only the wish of those who remain.

sentences.zh: 吾窮疾之人，平生意志，弟實知之。

translations.literal: I, a man exhausted by illness—my lifelong intent younger brother truly knew.
translations.idiomatic: I, a man broken by illness—my lifelong intent my brother truly knew.

sentences.zh: 端坐向窗，有何慰適，正賴弟耳。

translations.literal: Sitting upright facing the window, what comfort and ease—truly relying on younger brother only.
translations.idiomatic: Sitting upright by the window, what comfort is there—I truly relied on my brother alone.

sentences.zh: 過中未來，已自愒望，今云何得立，自省惛毒，無復人理。

translations.literal: Past noon he did not come—I was already weary with hope; now how can I stand? Examining myself, dim poison—no more human reason.
translations.idiomatic: Past noon he did not come and I was already weary with waiting; now how can I stand? Reflecting on myself in dim anguish—I am no longer human.

sentences.zh: 比煩冤困憊，不能作刻石文，若靈響有識，不得吾文，豈不為恨。

translations.literal: Lately vexed, wronged, exhausted and weary, unable to make inscribed stone text—if the spirit's echo has awareness and does not receive my text, would it not be regret?
translations.idiomatic: Lately vexed and exhausted, I cannot compose an inscription; if your spirit has awareness and does not receive my words, would that not be regret?

sentences.zh: 儻意慮不遂，謝能思之如狂，不知所告訴，明書此數紙，無復詞理，略道阡陌，萬不寫一。

translations.literal: If intent and thought are not fulfilled, Xie can think of it like madness, not knowing whom to tell; clearly writing these several sheets, no more words and reason, briefly telling paths between fields—ten thousand not written one.
translations.idiomatic: If my thoughts cannot be fulfilled, Xie can think of it like madness, not knowing whom to tell; plainly writing these sheets without order or reason, briefly tracing our paths—of ten thousand things not one is written.

sentences.zh: 阿謙！

translations.literal: Ah, Qian!
translations.idiomatic: Ah, Qian!

sentences.zh: 何圖至此！

translations.literal: Who planned it would come to this!
translations.idiomatic: Who dreamed it would come to this!

sentences.zh: 誰復視我，誰復憂我！

translations.literal: Who again will regard me, who again will worry for me!
translations.idiomatic: Who will look upon me again, who will care for me again!

sentences.zh: 他日寶惜三光，割嗜好以祈年，今也唯速化耳。

translations.literal: Other days I treasured the three lights, cut off preferences to pray for years—now only swift transformation.
translations.idiomatic: Other days I treasured sun, moon, and stars and gave up pleasures to pray for long life—now I wish only swift dissolution.

sentences.zh: 吾豈復支，冥冥中竟復云何。

translations.literal: How can I again support myself—in the dark dark what again will it be?
translations.idiomatic: How can I go on—in the darkness what will become of us?

sentences.zh: 弟懷隨、和之寶，未及光諸文章，欲收作一集，不知忽忽當辦此不？

translations.literal: Younger brother held the treasures of Sui and He, not yet reaching to illumine the various writings; I wished to gather them into one collection—do you know whether in haste this can be done?
translations.idiomatic: Brother held treasures like those of Sui and He, not yet brought to light in writing; I wished to gather his works into one collection—will it be done in time?

sentences.zh: 今已成服，吾臨靈取常共飲杯，酌自釀酒，寧有仿像不？

translations.literal: Now mourning garments are complete; I approach the spirit and take the cup we often drank together, pour self-brewed wine—is there perhaps some likeness?
translations.idiomatic: Now in mourning dress, I approach the spirit and take the cup we often shared, pour wine I brewed myself—is there perhaps some likeness of you?

sentences.zh: 冤痛！

translations.literal: Wronged pain!
translations.idiomatic: Wronged pain!

sentences.zh: 冤痛！

translations.literal: Wronged pain!
translations.idiomatic: Wronged pain!

sentences.zh: 元嘉三十年，卒，時年三十九。

translations.literal: In the thirtieth year of Yuanjia he died, aged thirty-nine.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the thirtieth year of Yuanjia, at the age of thirty-nine.

sentences.zh: 僧謙卒後四旬而微終。

translations.literal: Forty days after Sengqian's death Wei ended.
translations.idiomatic: Wei died forty days after Sengqian.

sentences.zh: 遺令薄葬，不設轜旐鼓挽之屬，施五尺床，為靈二宿便毀。

translations.literal: His final command was simple burial, not setting out funeral carts, banners, drums, or pulling teams; provide a five-foot couch; after two nights at the spirit, destroy it.
translations.idiomatic: His final instructions were for a simple burial, without funeral carts, banners, drums, or processions; provide a five-foot couch; after two nights before the spirit, destroy it.

sentences.zh: 以嘗所彈琴置床上，何長史來，以琴與之。

translations.literal: Place the zither he once played on the couch; when Chief Clerk He comes, give him the zither.
translations.idiomatic: Place the zither he once played on the couch; when Chief Clerk He comes, give him the zither.

sentences.zh: 何長史者，偃也。

translations.literal: Chief Clerk He was Yan.
translations.idiomatic: Chief Clerk He was He Yan.

sentences.zh: 無子。

translations.literal: He had no sons.
translations.idiomatic: He left no sons.

sentences.zh: 家人遵之。

translations.literal: The family followed this.
translations.idiomatic: The family followed his instructions.

sentences.zh: 所著文集傳於世。

translations.literal: The collected writings he authored were transmitted in the world.
translations.idiomatic: His collected writings circulated in the world.

sentences.zh: 世祖即位，詔曰：「微棲志貞深，文行惇洽，生自華宗，身安隱素，足以賁茲丘園，惇是薄俗。

translations.literal: When Shizu took the throne an edict said: "Wei dwelt with intent pure and deep, literary conduct sincere and harmonious, born from a splendid clan, personally at ease in plain simplicity—enough to adorn these hills and gardens and thicken this thin custom."
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Shizu ascended the throne, an edict read: "Wei dwelt with pure and deep intent, his literary conduct sincere and harmonious; born of a great clan, he lived at ease in plain simplicity—enough to adorn these hills and gardens and enrich this shallow age."

sentences.zh: 不幸蚤世，朕甚悼之。

translations.literal: Unfortunate early death—I deeply mourn him.
translations.idiomatic: He died untimely, and I deeply mourn him.

sentences.zh: 可追贈秘書監。」

translations.literal: He may be posthumously awarded Director of the Secretariat."
translations.idiomatic: Let him be posthumously awarded Director of the Secretariat."

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：燕太子吐一言，田先生吞舌而死；

translations.literal: The historiographer says: The Crown Prince of Yan spoke one word and Master Tian swallowed his tongue and died;
translations.idiomatic: The historiographer says: The Crown Prince of Yan spoke one word, and Master Tian swallowed his tongue and died;

sentences.zh: 安邑令戒屠者，閔仲叔去而之沛。

translations.literal: the magistrate of Anyi warned the butcher, and Min Zhongshu left and went to Pei.
translations.idiomatic: the magistrate of Anyi warned the butcher, and Min Zhongshu left for Pei.

sentences.zh: 良由內懷耿介，峻節不可輕干。

translations.literal: Truly because inwardly they harbor upright integrity—lofty integrity cannot be lightly offended.
translations.idiomatic: Truly because inwardly they harbor upright integrity—lofty integrity cannot be lightly offended.

sentences.zh: 袁淑笑謔之間，而王微弔詞連牘，斯蓋好名之士，欲以身為珪璋，皦皦然使塵玷之累，不能加也。

translations.literal: Between Yuan Shu's laughter and jest, Wang Wei's condolence words linked sheets—this is probably a man who loves fame, wishing to make his person jade regalia, bright and clear so that the burden of dust and stain cannot be added.
translations.idiomatic: Between Yuan Shu's laughter and jest, Wang Wei produced condolence letters sheet after sheet—such men love fame and wish to make themselves jade regalia, bright and clear so that the stain of dust cannot touch them.
